advances: A comparison envelope for arbitrary interior-convergent current parameters at fixed sampled certificate marks.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Each old mark remains interior, since Hausdorff convergence of convex bodies preserves any compact subset of the interior. For each $z$ take a fixed old center with a common interior ball of radius $r$ inside its current fiber and choose $R$ bounding distances to the center. Express the center as a convex combination of any sampled current point and the opposite point at radius $r$. The coefficient on the current point is at least $r/(R+r)$. Positivity and concavity bound the current fiber maximum by $(1+R/r)$ times the center value, and the center values are bounded by interior convergence. In a fixed current inball of radius $r_i$ about $Y_i$, a continuous-coordinate supergradient of $U_t$ has norm at most $U_t(Y_i)/r_i$ by positivity in the opposite gradient direction.

Apply 155691fc3768c06f on the hypograph-lift fibers $\{(X,s):X\in K_z(t),0\le s\le U_t(z,X)\}$ with supporting direction proportional to $(-c_{i,t},1)$, where $c_{i,t}$ is the chosen own-coordinate supergradient. The lifts have anchored compatibility and are positive compact convex bodies. After rescaling the direction to its original length, the support values are $\max_{X\in K_z(t)}(U_t(z,X)-c_{i,t}\cdot X)$, which are uniformly bounded. The fixed-matrix slope bound in the accepted proof supplies uniformly bounded base slopes touching at $p_i$. Adding back the continuous term gives the required affine planes with bounded coefficients, each sampled-majorizing and touching at its own $Y_i$. Their minimum has all the stated current inequalities and is positive on $C_t$ by affinity of the constituents.

On a subsequence any convergent plane array yields a minimum $V$ with $V\ge L$ at old sampled interior points by eventual membership and interior convergence, hence on $S$ by continuity. Also $V(Y_i)=L_i$. The inequality in b817b4ab3e2256b0 applies, since $V\ge L>0$ on the samples makes all its affine planes positive on the old hull. It gives $M^{-1}\int_S\log(V/L)\,dm\le0$. The integrand is nonnegative, so $V=L$ throughout each sampled fiber, by continuity and positive volume in every neighborhood of its points. This holds for every convergent plane array, proving uniform convergence on $S$ and giving a finite-plane representative there. Uniform Lipschitz bounds and Hausdorff convergence extend the comparison to $S_t$ using $L_{\rm ref}$. Since $\min_S L>0$, these comparisons imply a common positive floor and hence uniform convergence of the logarithms. Affinity yields positivity also on the old hull for all small $t$.
statement: Let $P$ be a nonempty finite base with positive compact convex $d$-fibers $K_z$, $d\ge1$, which are the actual sampled fibers of their lifted convex hull $C$. Let $S$ be the sampled union, with $dm$ the sum of fiber volumes and $M=m(S)$. Let $L$ be positive continuous concave on $C$, with $\int_S\log L\,dm=0$. Suppose finitely many own-interior marks $Y_i=(p_i,y_i)$ have positive weights $\sigma_i$ summing to one and probability rows $\rho_i$ on $S$ with means $Y_i$, means $L_i=L(Y_i)$ for $L$, and $\sum_i(\sigma_i/L_i)\rho_i=dm/(ML)$. Let compatible positive fibers $K_z(t)$ on the same finite base converge in Hausdorff distance to $K_z$. Use subscripts $t$ for the new hull, samples and volume, and let $U_t>0$ be continuous concave on $C_t$, with $\int_{S_t}\log U_t\,dm_t=0$. Assume $U_t\to L$ uniformly at the same coordinates on every compact subset of each old sampled fiber interior. For small $t$ there are uniformly bounded affine coefficient arrays $A_{i,t}$, one per old source, whose minimum $V_t$ is positive on both old and current hulls, dominates $U_t$ on $S_t$, and has $V_t(Y_i)=U_t(Y_i)$ at all fixed marks. Writing $L_{\rm ref}(z,X)=L(z,\operatorname{proj}_{K_z}X)$ on sampled base labels, both $V_t$ and its logarithm converge uniformly to $L_{\rm ref}$ and its logarithm on $S\cup S_t$. Also $L|_S$ has a representative that is the minimum of at most the number of sources affine planes.
title: Uniform positive touching envelopes for moving sampled fibers
